text:
maria: quick heads-up — p50 on the attention hotpath jumped ~12ms for some seq-length slices after yesterday's runtime deploy (seen on canary + a few prod traces). cc @jordan @perf-bot

jordan: thx — is this KV warm or cold? batch sizes? which model variant?

maria: observed on redwood-flash-v2; batch=8 in our perf harness; KV warm in most traces (we saw both but warm shows the regression too). baseline p50 ~18ms -> now ~30ms for seq in ~512-2048 bucket.

perf-bot: commit-range: 0a1b2c..1f2e3d introduced selector tweak (prefer fused-attn for certain shapes). perf-delta: +10.8ms p50 on attn hotpath (bench harness 2026-11-02).

kevin: looks like the selector change is the prime suspect. Can we bisect to the exact commit and repro locally?

sam: I have a small repro script for kernels: `./bench_attn --model redwood-flash-v2 --batch 8 --seq 1024 --kv-warm --runs 50 --force-seed 42` — use `--force-kernel=paged-flash|fused-attn|flashattn` to compare.

ciara: profiler flamegraph shows an extra memcpy and a small spike in kernel launch overhead when fused-attn path is chosen. attaching small excerpt: ```
# flame summary (top)
FusedAttnKernel      62.3%  (includes memcpy boundary) 
PagedFlashKernel     35.1%
memcpy H2D/D2H        2.6%
```

maria: ran sam's command on canary node and forced kernels: results (median over 50 runs): `fused-attn` = 31.2ms, `paged-flash` = 18.9ms, `flashattn` = 20.3ms. KV-warm. Re-running with KV-cold yields similar relative gap but higher absolute.

jordan: that's a clear signal. Do we know why fused path regresses? occupancy? extra staging buffer? ciara pointed to memcpy — would like a kernel-level trace.

ciara: dug in — fused-attn code path added a small staging buffer for short sequences to avoid bank conflicts; for seq ~1024 it triggers an extra device->device memcpy to align tiles. That memcpy wasn't present on paged-flash. Also launch config changed to grid-size X which reduces occupancy by ~10% for these shapes.

kevin: strategy: 1) bisect to the exact commit that added the staging/memcpy + launch tweak; 2) add targeted perf test to CI for seq=512/1024 batch=8; 3) temporary selector policy to prefer paged for seq >=256 until fix.

sam: starting a git bisect on the runtime branch now (range 0a1b2c..1f2e3d). I'll run the bench harness per-commit and report. expect ~3-5 commits to check.

perf-bot: scheduled bisect job #452 for bench-harness with params {model:redwood-flash-v2,batch:8,seq:1024,kv:warm}. Results will post here.

maria: quick mitigation — I pushed a runtime flag `--kernel-selector-override=prefer-paged-for-seq>=256` to canary and traffic A/B shows latency back to baseline for affected buckets. Not ideal long-term but buys time.

jordan: thanks. once sam finds the commit, let's get a small PR removing the memcpy and adjust tiling for those shapes. ciara, can you propose a patch that avoids device memcpy (maybe use shared mem or adjust indexing)?

ciara: I have two options: (A) adjust tiling to avoid staging for mid-sized sequences (likely low-risk), (B) replace D2D memcpy with an in-kernel copy using shared memory (higher perf but needs careful bank handling). I'll prototype A first.

sam: bisect update: landed on commit 0b7c9f which introduces both the staging buffer and the new grid calc. Repro script shows +11ms p50 at that commit.

kevin: open a bug, link commit and perf vectors, mark P0 for SLA impact. Add rollback as option if rollout worsens.

maria: created issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RI-1234 — includes traces, perf numbers, commit 0b7c9f, and canary rollback instructions.

sam: bisect job finished and posted full data to the issue (bench logs + nvprof traces).

jordan: next steps: CI perf test for seq=256/512/1024, ensure selector has a configurable threshold, prioritize ciara's tiling patch. Also add a quick e2e canary to verify no regression for smaller seqs.

maria: will coordinate the canary A/B, and will keep the selector override in place until we have the patch validated.

perf-bot: action items logged: #452 bisect done, issue RI-1234 opened, canary override applied. Closing thread when patch lands. :white_check_mark:
